Edge 2 only reaches the output through edge 5, so it is most useful when edge 5 is a strong conv.
A strong conv on the direct edge 3 already supplies high capacity, making the interior 3x3 on edge 2 largely redundant.
Removing edge 2 costs less when edge 4 provides a parallel conv route from node 1 to the output.
With no direct edge 3, all signal must pass through convolved routes, so adding capacity on edge 1 matters more.
A 3x3 on edge 2 makes edge 0's output feed a strong series route, so channel mixing on edge 0 is exploited more.
A conv on 0->2 already offers a high-capacity parallel path to the output, so upgrading the direct edge shows diminishing returns.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is fed only by edge 2, so a strong conv there supplies the only learned input to edge 5.
Dropping the direct edge hurts less when a conv route through node 2 already reaches the output.
